previews.title: fix(appimage): arm64 programs use the session's GL libraries over bundled copies
previews.summary: Some arm64 AppImages bundle GLVND frontends (libGLESv2.so.2, libEGL.so.1, ...) even though the AppImage excludelist says they must come from the system. The bundled copy is found first through the program's RUNPATH. It then runs on the session's libGLdispatch and Mesa EGL vendor, from a different GLVND release. Every GL call returns nothing, and the program crashes on its first GL query.
previews.author: maxjivi05

previews.title: fix(fex): x86 programs that use libOpenGL load again

previews.title: fix(nativeguest): keep parent lookups inside the guest root
previews.summary: ARMSX2 aborts after AppImage extraction in a session without proot: Assertion 'pathisabsolute(p)' failed ... chase(). Opening .. relative to a descriptor for the guest root reaches the Android parent directory. libudev therefore does not recognize the descriptor as the root and returns a relative path where systemd requires an absolute one.

previews.title: feat(files): add a plain text editor to the file manager
previews.summary:
• Tapping a file in browse mode (or the new first ⋮ menu item, Open) opens it in a full-screen plain text editor.
• Editing area: monospace body with a line-number gutter (cursor line highlighted), auto-scroll that keeps the cursor line in view, horizontal scrolling for long lines (no wrapping), and a status bar with Ln x, Col y, encoding and size; the file name gets a "• Modified" marker while dirty.
• Find/replace bar: live search with a match counter (n/m), previous/next with wrap-around, Aa case toggle, Replace (current match) and All; the current match is selected and scrolled into view.
• Every file is attempted regardless of extension: binary (NUL in the first 8 KB), over 512 KB, or non-writable files open read-only with a small chip; over 4 MB is refused with an inline message; back with unsaved changes asks for confirmation.
• Saving preserves the original encoding (UTF-8 → GB18030 → lossy UTF-8) and is atomic (temp file + rename); failure shows a toast. windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize" was added so the soft keyboard resizes the editor instead of covering it.

previews.title: feat(display): zero-copy presentation toggle and compositor display buffers
previews.summary:
• A Zero-copy presentation switch under Steam Settings > Display > Session Display, on by default, translated in every locale.
• A display-buffer allocator in the compositor. A Linux Vulkan driver whose metadata states displayBuffers asks it, over a socket in the session's runtime directory, for the memory behind the colour images it exports. The frames the nested compositor presents are then gralloc buffers, and the app's compositor puts them on the display layer as they are instead of copying them into its own swapcha
• Compressed (UBWC) buffers are offered only when the device allocator's sizes match the layout the drivers render to, which is probed once. Buffers that do not match are refused and the driver allocates as before.
• When an overlay above the game would need a display layer the panel cannot compose in hardware, the compositor tells gamescope how many planes it can show directly (new waylandoverlayplanes setting, gamescope patch 0135). gamescope then composes its overlays (performance overlay, client menus) into the game picture, which still reaches the display without a copy. Any other window above the g
• Buffers a client rendered straight into are held until the display's release fence signals, instead of going back with the fence attached to the dma-buf, which the kernel driver does not wait on. gamescope composites only into output images the compositor has released (patch 0136). This removes flickering dark lines seen while the panel was still reading a buffer being redrawn.
• Scaling, generated frames and HDR stay on the display layer, so turning one of them on no longer drops the session back to the copy path. The HDR switch reads HDR on a panel that can show it and Fake HDR otherwise.

tests.title: fix(desktop): package updates that set file capabilities finish without proot
tests.summary:
In Discover, Update All left snapd half-configured: "old snapd package postinst maintainer script subprocess failed with exit status 1". snapd's postinst runs setcap -q - /usr/lib/snapd/snap-confine, and that fails for two reasons:
• divertto replaced the diverted path with a symlink. setcap lstat()s its target and refuses anything that is not a regular file ("Invalid file ... for capability operation").
• Even on a regular file, Android rejects security.capability writes ("Operation not permitted"), so the native userland failed where proot's fake root did not.
